# Computation

The computation is `annual_average()` in
[`summary.py`](/references/computations/bocrates/src/bocrates/summary.py):
the mean overnight rate per calendar year, from dated observations. It is
a pure function — everything arrives as an argument, everything leaves as
a return value — which is what makes it testable, and the reason the
analysis script that reads the file and writes the output is a separate
file.

It declares **no parameters**. The data is fixed and committed, so the
result is a function of that data alone; there is nothing for an agent to
supply and nothing for it to edit.

## Running it

Follow [the executor](/references/executors/run-bocrates.md). Standard
library only, Python 3.11+. It prints a receipt carrying the SHA-256 of
the computation and of the data, and the result.

## Checking a run

Pass the receipt to [the attester](/references/attesters/bocrates-attester.py).
It re-hashes the bundled code and data, re-runs the computation, and
reports a verdict.

## The rest of the tree

The whole example project is under `references/computations/bocrates/`:
`data/`, `src/`, `tests/`, `analysis/`, `pyproject.toml`, `pixi.toml`,
`pixi.lock` and `CITATION.cff`. Its own `pixi run all` runs the tests and
regenerates `outputs/`. The example's README is not carried, because a
markdown file without frontmatter would break bundle conformance; this
concept is its description.
